name: Lolopo

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Lolopo (lolo1259).

notes: Lolopo / Yao'an Central Yi (Loloish, Sino-Tibetan) of Yunnan, China, in the Roman practical orthography developed by W. Scott Merrifield, in which speakers call their own speech ⟨Loxrlavu⟩. The Yi syllabary is a SEPARATE writing system for the Yi languages and is not mapped here (see the `ii` spec). INPUT CONTRACT: Loxrlavu-orthography Lolopo. CONSONANTS (Merrifield 2010, Table 5): voiced stops/affricates are written DOUBLE — ⟨bb dd gg zz jj⟩ = /b d ɡ dz dʒ/ — voiceless unaspirated single ⟨b d g z j⟩ = /p t k ts tʃ/, and voiceless aspirated ⟨p t k c q⟩ = /pʰ tʰ kʰ tsʰ tʃʰ/. ⟨s ss⟩ = /s z/, ⟨x⟩ = /ʃ/, ⟨y⟩ = /ʝ/, ⟨h hh⟩ = /x~h ɣ/, ⟨ng⟩ = /ŋ/, ⟨l⟩ = /l~ɮ/. TONE IS WRITTEN WITH LETTERS, and they are mapped: a syllable-final ⟨l⟩ is the HIGH tone 55, ⟨r⟩ the LOW tone 21, and an unmarked syllable is MID 33 (Merrifield 2010 §2.1.1). ⟨x⟩ additionally marks the TIGHT-THROAT (tense) register, which raises the mid and high tones (⟨x⟩ = 44, ⟨xl⟩ = 66) and adds a syllable-final glottal stop to the low tone (⟨xr⟩ = 21 with /ʔ/). ⟨l⟩ and ⟨x⟩ are onsets before a vowel and tone letters elsewhere, which `positional_graphemes` decides; likewise ⟨xl xr⟩ are the tense tone digraphs only in a rime (⟨vixlux⟩ [vi̠⁴⁴ɮɤ̠⁴⁴]). VOWELS: the seven lax vowels ⟨i ei ae a e o u⟩ = /i e æ a ɯ o u/ (with ⟨u⟩ realised [ɤ] in the transcriptions modelled here) and the diphthongs ⟨ie iae ia io ua⟩ = /ʲɛ ʲæ ʲa ʲo ʷa/; ⟨iu⟩ is the variant spelling of ⟨io⟩ used in the Wiktionary corpus. A high vowel after a sibilant or affricate apicalises ([z̩], [z̩ʷ]) and ⟨e⟩ after a coronal centralises to [ə] — both in the rule layer, not enumerated. A word-initial vowel takes an epenthetic /ʔ/.
